Stomata both on upper and lower sides

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The echinoderms are
questions.solution: Echinoderms are marine, spiny skinned animals. All members of phylum-Echinodermata are marine. These have water vascular system which helps in locomotion, eg, starfish, Antedon. Arboreal insect are insects, which living on trees. Freshwater forms are animals or plants living in freshwater of ponds, eg, Hydrilla.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Pneumatic bones are expected to be found in
questions.solution: Bones of Aves (eg, pigeon) are pneumatic. Pneumatic bones contain air cavities to reduce weight, which help in aerial mode of life.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following have notochord throughout life?
questions.solution:
Notochord is present in any stage of life of a chordate. It is replaced by vertebral column in vertebrates. Notochord is present throughout life in members of subphylum Cephalochordata, eg, Amphioxus.
In birds, fishes and snakes, notochord is replaced by vertebral column.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which is common between earthworm, leech and centipede?
questions.solution: Ventral nerve cord possesses segmental ganglia. It is common between earthworm, leech and centipede.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Tube feet is the locomotory organ of
questions.solution: Tube feet are extensible tubular processes bearing suckers and present in rows on the under-surface of echinoderms. Tube feet are connected internally with water vascular system. Each tube foot has an ampulla, a podium and a sucker. Tube feet are sensory structures that take part in adhesion, locomotion, respiration and food capturing. They are locomotory organs of echinoderms like starfish. Jelly fish is a member of phylum-Coelenterata. Scoliodon is a fish and silver fish is an arthropod.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Shell of molluscs is derived from
questions.solution: Molluscs are the soft bodied, unsegmented animals covered by a shell. In between the shell and body wall, is a covering called mantle, which secretes the shell.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During strenuous exercise, glucose is converted into
questions.solution: During strenuous exercise, deficiency of oxygen takes place. So, anaerobic respiration of glucose takes place. During anaerobic respiration, pyruvic acid (a product of glycolysis of glucose) change into lactic acid. Accumulation of lactic acid is responsible for muscle fatigue. Glycogen is a polysaccharide and storing material of animal body. Glycogen stored in muscle and liver. Starch is a polysaccharide and storing material of plant body.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one is component of Ornithine cycle?
questions.solution: Ornithine cycle or Krebs-Henseleit cycle or urea cycle was discovered by Hans Krebs andKurt Henseleit. It takes place in liver cells for synthesis of urea. The main component of ornithine cycle are arginine, ornithine and citrulline.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following amino acids is not optically active?
questions.solution: Glycine is the simplest and smallest amino acid. A compound shows optical activity, when a chiral carbon or asymmetrical carbon (ie, carbon which attached to four different groups or atoms) is present. Because chiral carbon is absent in glycine. So, it does not show optical activity. Other amino acids contain at least single asymmetric carbon atoms, so they show optical activity, eg, valine, leucine and isoleucine.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Balbiani rings are the structural features of
questions.solution: Balbiani rings are large RNA puffs reported in the salivary gland chromosomes of Chironomus insect during larval development.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Aspirin is a/an
questions.solution: Antipyretic drug is the drug which decreases body temperature, eg, aspirin. Antibiotics are drugs, which inhibit growth of microorganism, eg, penicillin. Antiseptics are substances which desroy the living organism from living surfaces like skin, eg, Savlon.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Chicory powder which is mixed with coffee powder is obtained from
questions.solution: Chicory powder is a flavouring material, which is mixed with coffee powder (from seeds of Coffea arabica). It is obtained from roots of Cichorium intybus of family-Compositae. Tea is dried leaves of Thea sinensis (family Theaceae). Ephedrine is obtained from stem of Ephedra gerardiana. It is useful against asthma and as cardiac stimulant.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Endoplasmic reticulum is in continuation with
questions.solution: Endoplasmic reticulum is the network of delicate strands and vesicles which extends from cell membrane to nuclear membrane. It acts as a circulatory system of cell and is of two typesrough endoplasmic reticulum and smooth endoplasmic reticulum. Rough endoplasmic reticulum involves in protein synthesis along with attached ribosomes and smooth endoplasmic reticulum helps in lipid and steroid synthesis. Cell wall is the outermost covering of plant cell generally made up of cellulose. Golgi bodies are double membrane bound cell organelles of eukaryotic cells which consist of vesicle, tubule and cisternae. Mitochondria is a rod-shaped, double membrane bound cell organelles.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During the meiotic division, the
questions.solution: Meiotic division occurs in reproductive or germ cells. Four haploid cells are produced after meiosis, which are not identical to their parent cell. In this division, homologous chromosomes form bivalent by pairing, during zygotene stage of prophase-I and during anaphase-I. Homologous chromosomes of each bivalent start migrating towards opposite poles of the spindle, because of this separation of homologous chromosomes, each daughter cell receives a haploid group of segregated chromosomes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During the $\mathrm{G}_1$-phase of cell division
questions.solution: Cell division has two phase : (a) Karyokinesis : Division of nucleus (b) Cytokinesis : Division of cytoplasm. Karyokinesis also consists of two phase : (i) Interphase is a resting phase and consists of $\mathrm{G}_1, \mathrm{~S}$ and $\mathrm{G}_2$-phase. $\begin{array}{|c|l|} \hline \text{Phase} & \text{Activities} \\ \hline \mathrm{G}_1 & \text{RNA and proteins synthesis takes place} \\ \hline \mathrm{S} & \text{DNA replication takes place} \\ \hline \mathrm{G}_2 & \begin{array}{l} \text{Damaged DNA is repaired and division of} \\ \text{centrosomes takes place} \end{array} \\ \hline \end{array}$ (ii)M-phase represents the phase of actual division.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: From which of the following plant is a medicine for respiratory disorders obtained?
questions.solution: Ephidrine is obtained from several species of Ephedra of family-Ephideraceae. It is used in the treatment of respiratory disorders like cold, asthma, bronchial congestion.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Ozone depletion in stratosphere would result in
questions.solution: In the atmosphere (stratosphere), about 30 km above the surface of the earth, the ozone molecules $\left(\mathrm{O}_3\right)$ form an umbrella. It prevents the penetration of harmful ultra violet radiation from the sun and thus protects the life of the earth. It is now feared that there is danger of depletion of the ozone layer. The prime suspects of ozone thinning or depletion are chlorofluoro carbons (CFCs). Because it is odourless, invisible, that is why, it is widely used in domestic refrigerators and cold storage facilities. It is calculated that the depletion of ozone layer by $1 \%$ results in an increase in the incidence of skin cancer by $5 \%$ to $7 \%$.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Molybdenum causes
questions.solution: Molybdenum causes mottling (patches on green and non-green areas).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Edible part in 'sorosis', a composite fruit, is
questions.solution: Composite fruits develop from entire inflorescence, eg, syconus develops from hypanthodium, eg, banyan. Sorosis is the composite fruit develops from spike and catkin, eg, in pineapple. Sorosis fruit develops from catkin; and edible part of pineapple fruits is peduncle and perianth. Fleshy thalamus is an edible part of pear, apple fruit, ie, pome fruits. Cotyledons are edible part of cashewnut, ie, nut fruit. Endosperm is an edible part of caryopsis of wheat, rice, etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is a true nut?
questions.solution: Nut is a fruit develops from polycarpellary, superior ovary. The pericarp is hard, woody or leathery, eg, edible part of chestnut is cotyledons. Ground nut is lomentum in which edible part is seed. Walnut is a drupe fruit in which edible part is cotyledon. Pistachio is a drupe in which edible part is seed.

questions.solution: Edible dry fruit which is known as chilgoza is seed of Pinus gerardiana. Gymnosperms are plants in of which ovary is absent so, there is production of naked seeds, hence fruits are absent in gymnosperms. Seeds of Cycas are not edible.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Pappus is modified
questions.solution: The fruits of Asteraceae often possess pappus (which is a modification of persistent hairy calyx) which functions as a parachute for the dispersal of, eg, Sonchus, Tagstes. This dispersal mechanism is known as parachute mechanism. Censer mechanism for seed dispersal is found in poppy.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Trimerous flower, superior ovary and axile placentation is characteristics of
questions.solution: Monocot is characterised by trimerous flowers, fibrous roots, parallel venation of leaves, eg, Family-Liliaceae. Trimerous flower, superior ovary and axile placentation is characteristics of familyLiliaceae, eg, onion. Cucurbitaceae, Solanaceae and Compositae are dicot families characterised by tetra or pentamerous flowers, tap roots and reticulated venation of leaves.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Clinging roots are found in
questions.solution: Clinging roots are found is orchids, these roots grow as epiphytes upon the trunks or branches of trees. They hang freely in the air and absorb atmospheric moisture with the help of special sponge like tissue called velamen. Velamen is the modification of epidermis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Expanded green stem of Opuntia is called
questions.solution: Phylloclade is a modified stem or branch which may be flat or circular, fleshy, like green leaf, eg, Opuntia.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The bioassay of auxin is
questions.solution: Bioassay is the testing of biological activity of a substance by employing living material. Went used Avena sativa (oat) coleoptiles in a technique called Avena coleoptile curvature test. ABA or abscisic acid induces dormancy in buds, seeds and underground storage organs. Unorganised and undifferentiated mass of cells forms during culture of cells known as callus. In callus culture, shoot and root regenerations are controlled, generally by auxin and cytokinin balance.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Solarisation is
questions.solution: Photosynthesis starts at quite low intensity of light and very high intensity causes oxidation and destruction of pigments, enzymes and intermediates. This destruction known as solarisation. So, solarisation causes reduction in photosynthetic yields. Photoperiodism is the effect of duration of sunlight on plants for many processes like flowering.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A fern prothallus is bisexual. If fertilisation takes place between their gametes than it is known as
questions.solution: Self-fertilisation is the union of male and female gametes produced by the same individual, ie, from a bisexual individual. Cross-fertilisation is the fertilisation of male and female gametes produced by different individuals. Isogamous means fusion of isogametes (ie, of same morphology and physiology). Viviparous means giving birth to young ones.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Most primitive member, in which roots are nc present, is
questions.solution: Psilophytes are the oldest of seedless vascular plants. The plants are characterised by the absence of roots and presence of rhizoids, eg, Rhynia is the most primitive member of pteridophytes. Lycopodium and Selaginella are developed pteridophytes in which plant body is differentiated into roots, stems and leaves.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is not the feature of gymnosperms?
questions.solution: Gymnosperms (Gymno $=$ naked; sperma $=$ seed) are naked seed bearing perennial plants. In gymnosperms, there is no fruit formation (because ovary is absent); xylem without vessels and phloem without companion cells and have distinct branches.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During unfavourable conditions, the sponges for
questions.solution: Under unfavourable conditions like high temperature, dry condition, sponges body gets divided into numerous small spore like bodies called gemmules to tide over the adverse environmental conditions. Cysts are formed during unfavourable conditions in Amoeba. Spicules are endoskeletons of sponge body.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Decarboxylation is involved in
questions.solution: Decarboxylation is the removal of carbon from a compound to make carbon dioxide. During Krebs' cycle, the acetyl groups pass round the cycle, and the two carbon atoms are lost in the form of carbon dioxide in to decarboxylation reactions.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Stem cuttings are commonly used for the propagation of
questions.solution: Stem cuttings are used in rose, Citrus, Cocoa. Rooting of stem cuttings is hastened by dipping in NAA or IBA. Grafting is done in case of mango. Rhizomes take part in vegetative propagation due to presence of buds, eg, banana, ginger.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Ubisch bodies are present in
questions.solution: Ubisch bodies : Tapetum is the innermost layer of another wall which surrounds the sporogenous tissues. These cells are nutritive in function. In cells of tapetum, ubisch bodies are present, which help in the formation of microspore wall or exine of pollen grain. Pollen grain (microspore) is generally a round haploid structure from which gametophyte is developed. Pollen tube helps in carrying male gametes to female gamete for fertilisation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: An obligate root parasite is
questions.solution: Obligate parasites are organism which obtain their food from host throughout their life, eg, Rafflesia, Orobanche (root parasite). Facultative parasites are organism which are normally parasitic but can obtain their food from dead organic matter under certain conditions. Obligate root parasite Rafflesia, Orobanche. Partial stem parasite Viscum, Loranthus. Partial root parasite Santalum. Obligate stem parasite Cuscuta.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Ruminants belong to order
questions.solution: Ruminants have the habit of chewing the cud. Stomach of ruminants have four parts, ie, rumen, reticulum, omassum and abomassum. They belong to order-Artiodactyla of class-Mammalia, eg, cow, sheep, goat. Elephants belong to order-Proboscidea of class-Mammalia. Marsupials are the members of subclassMetatheria, in which a pouch marsupium is present for keeping and nourishing the young ones, eg, kangaroo.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Osmotic pressure of a solution is
options: less than or greater than pure solvent
questions.solution: Osmotic pressure of solution is greater than pure solvent. When a solution is separated from pure solvent by a semi-permeable membrane, the solvent begins to flow towards the solution due to development of osmotic pressure.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In which form does the food transported in plants?
questions.solution: Translocation is the movement of organic nutrients (ie, food) from the region of source or supply to the region of sink or utilisation. Translocation of food occurs through phloem. This organic food is translocated in the form of sucrose, a disaccharide, which is relatively inactive and highly soluble sugar.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following has the highest bond order ?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{N}_2\left(7+7=14 e^{-}\right)= & K K^*, \sigma 2 s^2, \stackrel{\star}{\sigma} 2 s^2, \pi 2 p_x^2 \\ \approx & \pi 2 p_y^2, \sigma 2 p_z^2 \\ \mathrm{BO}= & \frac{1}{2}(8-2)=3 \\ \mathrm{O}_2\left(8+8=16 e^{-}\right)= & K K^*, \sigma 2 s^2, \sigma_\sigma^* 2 s^2, \sigma 2 p_z^2, \\ & \pi 2 p_x^2 \approx \pi 2 p_y^2, \stackrel{*}{\pi} 2 p_x^1 \approx \pi 2 p_y^1 \\ \mathrm{BO}= & \frac{1}{2}(8-4)=2 \\ \mathrm{He}_2\left(2+2=4 e^{-}\right)= & \sigma 1 s^2, \sigma^* 1 s^2 \\ \mathrm{BO}= & \frac{1}{2}(2-2)=0\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the order of the reaction?
questions.solution:
Order of a reaction is the sum of the power to which the concentration terms are raised in the rate law equation to express the observed rate of the reaction.
Hence, order $=\frac{1}{2}+2=\frac{5}{2}=2.5$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: In long form of Periodic Table, the properties of the elements are a periodic function of their
questions.solution: In modern Periodic Table, the physical and chemical properties of the elements are a periodic function of their atomic number, ie, if the elements are arranged in order of their increasing atomic number, the elements with similar properties are repeated after certain regular intervals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.solution: Electronegativity, ionisation energy and electron affinity of $s$-block elements in their respective period is low but the atomic radius of the $s$-block elements is larger in their respective period due to less effective nuclear charge.

&

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The solubility of saturated solution of $\mathrm{Ag}_2 \mathrm{CrO}_4$ is $s$ mol $\mathrm{L}^{-1}$. What is its solubility product?
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{Ag}_2 \mathrm{CrO}_4$ ionises completely in the solution as
$\underset{s \mathrm{~mol} / \mathrm{L}}{\mathrm{Ag}_2 \mathrm{CrO}_4 \longrightarrow} \underset{2 s \mathrm{~mol} / \mathrm{L}}{2 \mathrm{Ag}^{+}}+\underset{s \mathrm{~mol} / \mathrm{L}}{\mathrm{CrO}_4^{2-}}$
Hence, the solubility product,
$\begin{aligned}
K_{\text {sp }} \text { of } \mathrm{Ag}_2 \mathrm{CrO}_4 & =\left[\mathrm{Ag}^{+}\right]^2\left[\mathrm{CrO}_4^{2-}\right] \\
& =(2 s)^2(s) \\
& =4 s^3
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a Lewis acid?
questions.solution: $\mathrm{OH}^{-}, \mathrm{F}^{-}$and $\mathrm{NH}_3$ are Lewis base because they can donate a lone pair of electrons while $\mathrm{H}^{+}$is a Lewis acid because it can accept a lone pair of electrons.

questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} \frac{p^{\circ}-p_s}{p^{\circ}}=\frac{n}{n+N} & =\frac{\frac{w}{m}}{\frac{w}{m}+\frac{W}{M}} \\ \because \quad \frac{w}{m} &  \lt \frac{W}{M} \\ \therefore \quad \frac{p^{\circ}-p_s}{p^{\circ}} & =\frac{w / m}{W / M}=\frac{w}{m} \times \frac{M}{W} \\ \frac{3000-2985}{3000} & =\frac{5}{m} \times \frac{18}{100} \\ m & =\frac{5 \times 18 \times 3000}{15 \times 100} \\ m & =180\end{aligned}$
180 is the molecular weight of glucose $\left(\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_{12} \mathrm{O}_6\right)$, thus the substance ' $X$ ' is glucose.

questions.q: A charge $q$ is located at the centre of a cube. The electric flux through any face is
questions.solution:

questions.q: Figure shows three spherical and equipotential surfaces $A, B$ and $C$ round a point charge $q$. The potential difference $V_A-V_B=V_B-V_C$. If $t_1$ and $t_2$ be the distances between them, then
questions.solution:
Potential difference between two equipotential surfaces $A$ and $B$,
$V_A-V_B=k q\left(\frac{1}{r_A}-\frac{1}{r_B}\right)=k q\left(\frac{r_B-r_A}{r_A r_B}\right)=\frac{k q t_1}{r_A r_B}$
or $\quad t_1=\frac{\left(V_A-V_B\right) r_A r_B}{k q}$
or
$t_1 \propto r_A r_B$
Similarly, $t_2 \propto r_B r_C$
Since, $r_A \lt r_B \lt r_C$, therefore, $r_A r_B \lt r_B r_C\therefore \quad t_1 \lt t_2$

questions.q: The neck and bottom of a bottle are 3 cm and 15 cm in radius respectively. If the cork is pressed with a force 12 N in the neck of the bottle, then force exerted on the bottom of the bottle is
questions.solution:
Pressure at neck of bottle
$p_1=\frac{F_1}{A_1}=\frac{F_1}{\pi r_1^2}$
Similarly, pressure at bottom of bottle
$p_2=\frac{F_2}{A_2}=\frac{F_2}{\pi r_2^2}$
According to Pascal's law, liquids transmit pressure equal in all directions.
$\therefore\begin{aligned}
\frac{F_1}{\pi r_1^2} & =\frac{F_2}{\pi r_2^2} \\
\frac{12}{\pi(3)^2} & =\frac{F_2}{\pi(15)^2} \\
F_2 & =\frac{12 \times 15 \times 15}{3 \times 3} \\
F_2 & =300 \mathrm{~N}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: 64 spherical rain drops of equal size are falling vertically through air with a terminal velocity $1.5 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$. If these drops coalesce to form a big spherical drop, then terminal velocity of big drop is
questions.solution:

The terminal velocity of spherical rain drop

\Rightarrow \quad & \frac{v_1}{v_2}=\left(\frac{r}{R}\right)^2=\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^2=\frac{1}{16} \\
\therefore \quad & v_2=16 v_1=16 \times 1.5=24 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If ${ }_{92} \mathrm{U}^{238}$ emits $8 \alpha$-particles and $6 \beta$-particles, then the resulting nucleus is
questions.solution:
After one $\alpha$-emission, the daughter nucleus reduces in mass number by 4 unit and in atomic number by 2 unit. In $\beta$-emission the atomic number of daughter nucleus increases by 1 unit. The reaction can be written as
${ }_{92} \mathrm{U}^{238} \xrightarrow{-8 \alpha}{ }_{76} X^{206} \xrightarrow{-6 \beta}{ }_{82} Y^{206}$
Thus, the resulting nucleus is ${ }_{82} Y^{206}, i e,{ }_{82} \mathrm{~Pb}^{206}$.

Hence, dimensions of $A B=\left[\mathrm{ML}^{5 / 2} \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]\left[\mathrm{M}^0 \mathrm{LT}^0\right]=\left[\mathrm{ML}^{7 / 2} \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The equation of a wave is $y=5 \sin \left(\frac{t}{0.04}-\frac{x}{4}\right)$; where, $x$ is in cm and $t$ is in second. The maximum velocity of the wave will be
questions.solution:
Equation of wave
$y=5 \sin \left(\frac{t}{0.04}-\frac{x}{4}\right)$
The standard equation of a wave in the given form is
$y=a \sin \left(\omega t-\frac{2 \pi x}{\lambda}\right)$
Comparing the given equation with the standard equation, we get
$a=5 \text { and } \omega=\frac{1}{0.04}=25$
Therefore, maximum velocity of particles of the medium,
$v_{\max }=a \omega=5 \times 25=125 \mathrm{cms}^{-1}=1.25 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$

Pure tall plants are crossed with pure dwarf plants. In the $\mathrm{F}_1$ generation, all plants were tall. These tall plants of $F_1$ generation were selfed and the ratio of tall to dwarf plants obtained was
$3: 1$. This is called
questions.solution: The phenotype produced by heterozygotes is identical with that produced by homozygous for the concerned dominant allele. The dominant allele in such a situation is known as completely dominant, eg, when pure tall plant is crossed with pure dwarf plant. In $F_1$ generation, all plants were tall. These tall plants of $\mathrm{F}_1$ generation were selfed than the ratio of tall to dwarf plants obtained was $3: 1$. So, allele of tallness is dominant to allele of dwarfness.
